source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
3. Identify the failed appliance: Record the make, model, serial number, and location of the appliance in your documentation. Include a brief description of the appliance and any identifying features if necessary. 

4. Document the failed safety checks systematically:
   a. List all safety checks that were performed on the appliance.
   b. For each safety check, specify whether the test passed or failed, and note the testing method used (e.g., visual inspection, functional test, measurement with a multimeter or PAT tester, etc.).
   
5. Detail the specific failure points: Describe the issues found. Specify whether the failure poses an immediate danger, needs minor repair, or requires replacement. 

6. Include readings and measurements: For checks involving electrical readings (e.g., insulation resistance, earth continuity), record the actual measurements obtained during the test.

7. Take photos and attach: Use a dated digital camera or a camera with timestamp capability to record images of
